# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 22 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 22 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_022_page_001.jpg

---

## Vision 4, Chapter 1

**1** The fourth vision, my friends, came twenty days after the third — a preview of the great tribulation that lies ahead. **2** I was out walking again on that country road, about ten stades from the main road, in rough country. **3** Walking alone, I was praying for the Lord to complete everything he had been showing me through his holy church — to strengthen me and to open the door of repentance to his servants who had fallen — so that his great and glorious name would be honored. After all, he had considered me worthy enough to show me his wonders. **4** While I was praising and thanking him, I heard something like a voice responding: "Don't be double-minded, Hermas." I thought, "How could I be double-minded? Look at everything God has shown me and done for me." **5** A little further on — brace yourselves, friends — I saw dust billowing up toward the sky. I thought, "Must be livestock." But the cloud was only about a stade away. **6** As it kept rising I realized this was no ordinary thing. The sun pierced through briefly and I saw it: a monstrous creature like an enormous sea-beast, its mouth pouring out fiery locusts. It was roughly a hundred feet long, its head shaped like a clay pot. **7** I broke into tears, desperately asking the Lord to deliver me. Then those words came back to me: "Don't be double-minded, Hermas." **8** So I did it. I wrapped myself in faith in the Lord, called up everything he had taught me, gathered my courage, and walked straight toward it. This thing was charging at the speed and power of something that could demolish an entire city. **9** But as I got close, the huge creature just flattened itself on the ground, stuck out its tongue, and didn't move — not until I had walked all the way past it. **10** Its head was painted in four colors: black, then fiery red mixed with blood, then gold, then white.

---

*PNEUMA note: Hermas walking toward a city-destroying monster armed only with faith is the defining image of the entire Shepherd — and perhaps of early Christian martyrdom theology. The beast does not harm those who do not doubt.*
